Did you know that one of the best treatments for back pain is actually free and requires no equipment? Walking is often overlooked, but as a specialized orthopedic spine surgeon, I frequently recommend it as a foundational pillar for spinal recovery and long-term health.
Here is how a daily walk protects your back:
Strengthens Core & Posture: Walking engages the muscles in your abdomen and lower back. These muscles act as a natural "brace" for your spine, reducing the load on your vertebral discs.
Boosts Circulation: Your spinal structures don't have a direct blood supply. Movement helps "pump" nutrient-rich blood and oxygen into the soft tissues and discs, accelerating healing.
Increases Flexibility: Regular movement improves your range of motion and prevents the stiffness that often leads to acute "catches" or muscle spasms.
Weight Management: Maintaining a healthy weight is vital. Every extra kilogram adds significant mechanical stress to the lumbar spine (lower back).
Tips for a Spine-Friendly Walk:
Wear Supportive Shoes: Good arch support reduces the impact traveling up to your back.

Neck pain and radiating arm pain are common symptoms of Cervical Degenerative Disc Disease (DDD), a natural age-related wear-and-tear condition of the spine. The cervical spine contains discs that act as shock absorbers between the vertebrae. Over time, these discs lose hydration, become thinner, and may lead to inflammation, reduced mobility, and nerve compression.
There are two main types of symptoms associated with cervical disc degeneration. Localized neck pain presents as stiffness, dull aching, muscle tightness, and difficulty in neck movements. In contrast, radicular pain, often described as a “pinched nerve,” occurs when a bulging disc or bone spur compresses nearby nerves. This can cause sharp, shooting pain radiating from the neck into the shoulder, arm, or fingers, along with tingling, numbness, and weakness.
Early recognition of these symptoms is important for timely treatment and prevention of progression. If you are experiencing persistent neck pain or electric shock-like sensations in your arm, consult a spine specialist for proper diagnosis and management.

owner_posts.post_text:
Not Every Joint Problem Needs the Same Treatment Approach

When dealing with joint pain, many people assume there is one best treatment. In reality, the right approach depends on the underlying condition, symptom severity, activity level, and individual treatment goals.

Two commonly discussed options in Orthopaedic care are Physiotherapy and Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) therapy. While both play an important role, they support recovery in different ways.

Physiotherapy may help by:
• Improving joint mobility and flexibility
• Strengthening muscles that support the joint
• Improving balance, movement, and function
• Supporting recovery after injury or surgery

PRP therapy may be considered to help support:
• Chronic tendon-related conditions
• Early joint degeneration and Osteoarthritis
• The body's natural healing response
• Pain reduction and improved function in suitable patients

In some cases, these approaches may complement each other as part of a broader treatment plan.

If Knee Pain, joint stiffness, reduced mobility, or a tendon-related problem is affecting your daily activities, and you are looking for guidance from an experienced Orthopedic Surgeon, you may consider visiting our clinic in Ghatkopar West, where care is provided under the guidance of Dr. Chintan Patel, with an individualized assessment based on your symptoms and treatment goals.

Understanding different treatment options can help you make informed decisions about your joint health.

Monsoon Slip and Fall Injuries: Prevention Is Better Than Recovery

The monsoon season brings welcome relief from the heat, but it also creates conditions that increase the risk of slips, falls, sprains, and fractures. Wet floors, slippery roads, uneven surfaces, and poor visibility can turn a routine walk into an unexpected injury.

A simple fall can affect the skin. Depending on the impact, injuries may involve bones, ligaments, tendons, muscles, or joints, sometimes leading to prolonged pain, swelling, and reduced mobility.

A few precautions can help reduce the risk:
• Wear footwear with a good grip and slip-resistant soles
• Walk carefully on wet tiles, stairs, and uneven surfaces
